system: WhatsApp channel to Vanessa — marcelrgberger/whatsapp-cli vs normen/whatscli
description: Both clients cloned and read in full 2026-09-22. whatsapp-cli (MIT, Python) reads the WhatsApp desktop app's local ChatStorage.sqlite read-only and sends via the whatsapp:// URL scheme + System Events; it exposes --json, monitor since <ts>, message get --after, message send, chat find and session status, so an unattended runner task can poll and reply. whatscli (MIT, Go, whatsmeow + tview) parses no flags and its README states 'No automation of messages, no sending of messages through shell commands' — nothing a task can call, and it emulates a linked device. Recommendation: whatsapp-cli. Task spec written as integrations/mac-task-specs.md §5 (cron 4-59/10, same inbound handler as the iMessage task, agentInbox shapes, allow-listed sender only); install guide MAC-INSTALL-comms-data.md §1; rows added to CONNECTIONS.md and REMOTE-ACCESS.md.
before: No WhatsApp path; the deck's note says WhatsApp was removed because personal accounts have no supported API.
after: whatsapp-cli recommended with reasons; spec, install, security section and deck row written; nothing installed or live.
haltReason: Needs Steven: a dedicated WhatsApp number (never the client-facing one), linking it in the WhatsApp desktop app on the Mac, granting Full Disk Access and Accessibility, and running the task once by hand.

system: whatsapp-cli send path vs headless runner
description: Reads are read-only SQLite (sqlite3 'file:…?mode=ro') and work headless with Full Disk Access; sends open whatsapp://send?… and press Return through System Events, which requires an awake Mac, a logged-in GUI session and Accessibility permission. A claude-runner task can therefore always read but may fail to send when the screen is locked. The spec handles it: reply kept as 'draft — send pending', three retries, then a Needs-Steven note on iMessage. `monitor auto-reply` (which shells out to claude -p on its own) is explicitly excluded because it bypasses the shared handler, HALT list and logging.
after: Send-failure handling and the auto-reply exclusion written into mac-task-specs.md §5.

system: PII policy for the free route — mode flag, deferral, canary (closes F-E8-60 once run)
description: While routed to free providers no client PII, loan-file text, CRM record, ISA-line content, credit or health data may leave the Mac. Written into the launcher as a mode flag every task can read (VANESSA_ROUTE_MODE, VANESSA_PII_OK, ~/.config/omniroute/state/mode): tasks in DEFAULT_PII_TASKS (Lofty/Zoho/ISA bridge/lead/inbox/health tasks) or ~/.config/omniroute/pii-tasks.txt are deferred with exit 75, or pinned to the local Jarvis model through OmniRoute when OMNIROUTE_LOCAL_MODEL is configured. A two-part PII canary (task-tagged run must exit 75 with zero requests at :20128; untagged run must be blocked by the existing guard hook, 'CANARY' absent from OmniRoute's log) is specified for the security steward.
before: One untested hook stood between client data and free third-party providers.
after: Launcher-level gate plus a canary test; F-E8-60 can be closed only after both canary halves pass on the Mac.
haltReason: The canary must be run on the Mac by Steven with the security steward before the runner is pointed at claude-auto.

description: A fetched README summary claimed OmniRoute reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY-style environment variables; a grep of the 3.8.50 source and docs found no such reader (only its own OMNIROUTE_API_KEY, telemetry TTLs and OAuth client ids). Keys enter through the dashboard or `omniroute providers add <id> --credential-env <NAME>` / `--credential-stdin`, stored encrypted in its SQLite. Documented accordingly: ~/.config/omniroute/.env holds NAME=value lines (chmod 600) that the CLI reads once; the launcher reads only OMNIROUTE_API_KEY from it.
before: Would have documented env vars OmniRoute ignores.
after: README and MAC-INSTALL-comms-data.md §2 name the real path.
